summary: MinSU Clearance System — iteration 3 brute-force + admin unlock coverage. Backend: 54/55 pytest pass (1 skipped last-admin guard, unchanged from iter2). Added new /app/backend/tests/test_bruteforce.py (10 tests, all PASS) covering: 4x401 then 429 lock on 5th attempt; correct-password blocked while locked; successful login clears lockout_until; unknown emails stay 401 (no auto-lock); user.locked audit entry written on threshold crossing; admin.unlock_user audit entry written; POST /api/admin/users/{id}/unlock returns 200 (admin), 403 (non-admin), 404 (unknown target); GET /api/admin/users includes is_locked boolean per user. Frontend: verified via Playwright — created victim via API, locked it with 5 wrong logins (got 401,401,401,401,429), logged in as admin, opened Users tab (nav-users), Users table renders Status column with red '🔒 Locked' badge and Unlock button for locked users. Clicking [data-testid='unlock-user-<id>'] triggers confirm dialog (auto-accepted), POSTs to /api/admin/users/{id}/unlock, shows 'Account unlocked' toast, and reloads with victim row now showing green 'Active' badge (no Unlock button). All regression flows still function. is_locked flag returned correctly from GET /api/admin/users.

minor.issue: Per-IP 20-failure secondary shield is enforced but only per rolling window; cannot be easily reset without direct DB access. If pytest runs many brute-force tests without purging audit_logs, the IP shield may trip and cause admin login attempts from the same IP to 429 too. Mitigated in test_bruteforce.py via _reset_ip_failures fixture.
Carried over: still accepts unknown user_id and returns success.

critical_code_review_comments: _check_bruteforce runs BEFORE any user lookup, so a locked account cannot leak timing info — good.

_register_failure counts the just-written failure audit as part of the threshold check (comment in code confirms). Threshold is `fails >= BRUTEFORCE_MAX_FAILURES` after the 5th failure has been written, which is correct.

Lockout state is stored on user document (lockout_until) AND derived from audit_logs count — dual source of truth. Successful login clears lockout_until but NOT the historical failure audit entries; the rolling window naturally lets them age out.
GET /api/admin/users correctly derives is_locked live from lockout_until vs now(), so a stale future timestamp on a user document surfaces as locked in UI — good.

admin_unlock_user only $unsets lockout_until/last_lockout_at; it does NOT purge the failure audit entries. This is arguably correct (audit history is immutable) but means an unlocked user whose failure count is still within the 15-min window will re-lock quickly if they mistype again. Consider clearing the failure counter for the user on manual unlock OR document the behaviour.
Frontend unlockUser() uses window.confirm — same UX as delete. data-testid='unlock-user-<uuid>' present and matched by test. Toast + row refresh work correctly.
No client-side rate-limiting on the Unlock button; rapid double-click could send two POSTs (both would 200 harmlessly, still not ideal).
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_bruteforce.py (NEW: 10 tests covering brute-force lockout + admin unlock + is_locked field)
seed_data_creation: Each brute-force test creates a fresh victim student (bf_victim_<runid>_<rand>@minsu.edu.ph) with password Correct1Pass. Fixture resets lockout + purges IP-failure audit entries between tests. UI test additionally creates one uix<ts>@minsu.edu.ph victim.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Brute-force config: MAX_FAILURES=5, WINDOW=15min, LOCKOUT=15min, IP_MAX_FAILURES=20. Lockout stored as ISO string in users.lockout_until; is_locked is derived live in /api/admin/users. To reset test state manually: db.users.updateOne({email:X},{$unset:{lockout_until:''}}); db.audit_logs.deleteMany({actor_email:X,status:'failure'}). To also clear IP shield: db.audit_logs.deleteMany({action:'user.login',status:'failure'}). Frontend selectors: [data-testid='users-table'], [data-testid='user-locked-badge'], [data-testid='unlock-user-<uuid>'], [data-testid='nav-users'], [data-testid='login-submit-button']. window.confirm is used for the unlock confirmation dialog (Playwright: page.on('dialog', d.accept())).
